investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was reported Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were fully exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule new agent pods. At the time of the eval run (2026-07-18T14:37–14:44Z), 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported it as fully consumed, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. Because the pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window (~133–144 s), the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885, createAgent call) never received a VM ID or a ready state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata peer-pods resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api Kubernetes cluster has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (source-context: infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the scheduler could not place the peer-pod VM on any of the 6 available nodes — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm quota and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — and preemption was not possible because no lower-priority victims existed on the eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 133–144 seconds across all three checks, causing the eval to time out before any agent identity or state could be captured, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod spawned by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that support the required VM type, and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4 nodes. No pod reached a running state, so no agent was ever created, and the expected-output contract received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the only 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every eval pod remains unscheduled until the probe timeout fires. This is a cluster-level infrastructure resource exhaustion localized to the remote-agent scheduling path; it is an eval-detected infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-traffic outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence).

If those 2 nodes are undersized for the expected concurrency, capacity will be exhausted under normal load.
